_doc: Internal names and retired claim-state on the published site (scripts/site_gates.py taxonomy-leaks; COO dispatch 2026-10-16, §15.10.767 §S.2 and §S.4; the reader test of 2026-10-16 §4).

A fail-tier rule fails the build on any match in a file it scans. A pending row holds the hits of ONE fail-tier rule inside ONE exact string in ONE file: an occurrence that has no ratified replacement yet. It is printed on every run, and it fails the build once the string no longer occurs (drop the row in the same change that ships the ratified string).

An allowlist row sanctions the hits of ONE fail-tier rule inside ONE occurrence of ONE ratified string in ONE file: a name the COO ruled stays where the string uses it (§15.10.773 §F.4; Copy Set §13 K: 'Hermes' is the public name of the contract surface at four occurrences only). Its source names the ruling. It fails the build when its string no longer occurs, occurs more than once, or holds no hit of its rule. The recurrence floor runs with the allowlist in place, so no row can sanction a bare recurrence.
Report-tier rules list what the COO has not ruled yet. They print on every run and fail nothing.

Every rule carries fixtures: the self-test seeds each one into a tree and proves the gate finds it (a fail-tier fixture fails the gate). near_misses are texts the rule must not find. files scopes a rule to the files named.

Governance references (lesson numbers, diligence names, internal document titles, cluster and rule numbers) are removed from public copy, not mapped (Copy Set §13 F). Component names are replaced only by a ratified string.

This list carries every entry of the shell step it replaces (Sacred Invariant, sacred_invariants, Pattern-32/43/50/65, THEMIS-DA-/Themis-DA-, Mnemosyne ledger, mnemosyne_ledger, Plutus orchestration, plutus_ring) as fixtures of the rules that now cover them.

Below this list sits a recurrence floor held in code (RECURRENCE_FLOOR in scripts/site_gates.py): every name, reference and retired claim above, and every shell-list marker, seeded alone into the published files, must fail this list. Dropping a rule, turning one to report, moving its scope, excluding a file or weakening a pattern together with its own fixtures fails the self-test.
